Music recordings and acoustic features

acoustic_brainz.Rd

A dataset of songs with their acoustic features. The data combine AcousticBrainz audio analyses with MusicBrainz canonical recording metadata. The data was filtered to only contain a select number of artists and only up to 25 songs per artist.

Usage

acoustic_brainz

Format

A tibble with 24 variables:

recording_mbid

MusicBrainz identifier for the canonical recording. Identifies a particular recording rather than a musical composition in general.

target_artist

Artist name.

release_mbid

MusicBrainz identifier for the release metadata record.

artist

Artist credit from MusicBrainz.

song

Recording title from MusicBrainz.

release

Release title from MusicBrainz. This is not necessarily the recording's first release.

key

Estimated musical key, expressed as a pitch-class name such as C or F#. Taken from the first retained acoustic analysis within each canonical recording.

scale

Estimated musical scale, typically major or minor. Taken from the first retained acoustic analysis within each canonical recording.

average_loudness

Normalized loudness descriptor on a scale from 0 to 1. Higher values indicate less dynamic range. This is not a loudness measurement in decibels.

dynamic_complexity

Descriptor of loudness fluctuations, based on average absolute deviation from estimated global loudness on the decibel scale. Higher values indicate greater fluctuation.

mfcc_zero_mean

Mean of the zeroth mel-frequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC), as supplied in the AcousticBrainz feature dump. A technical descriptor derived from the audio spectrum.

bpm

Estimated tempo in beats per minute.

bpm_first_peak_mean

Source-reported mean tempo at the highest peak of the BPM histogram, in beats per minute.

bpm_first_peak_median

Source-reported median tempo at the highest peak of the BPM histogram, in beats per minute.

bpm_second_peak_mean

Source-reported mean tempo at the second-highest peak of the BPM histogram, in beats per minute.

bpm_second_peak_median

Source-reported median tempo at the second-highest peak of the BPM histogram, in beats per minute.

danceability

Algorithmic estimate of danceability. Higher values indicate greater estimated danceability. This is neither a probability nor a human rating.

onset_rate

Number of detected sound onsets per second, describing how frequently new sound events begin.

tuning_frequency

Estimated reference tuning frequency, in hertz.

tuning_equal_tempered_deviation

Descriptor of deviations of spectral pitch-profile peaks from equal-tempered pitch positions. Higher values indicate greater deviation.

n_acoustic_recordings

Number of retained AcousticBrainz recording analyses combined to create the row. Only the first submission for each original recording identifier is considered.

Source

AcousticBrainz low-level, rhythm, and tonal feature dumps dated June 23, 2022: https://acousticbrainz.org/download

MusicBrainz Canonical Data Dumps, using canonical_recording_redirect.csv and canonical_musicbrainz_data.csv: https://metabrainz.org/datasets/download

The source acoustic data and MusicBrainz core metadata were released under CC0. Preparation code and source-file details are provided in the package repository's data-raw directory.

Details

Selection and matching

Artists were selected using the preparation file artists-to-select.csv found in the R package data-raw folder. MusicBrainz artist credits were matched to this list using case-insensitive matching after trimming leading and trailing whitespace. When multiple metadata rows were available for a recording, the row with the highest metadata score was retained.

Original recording identifiers were linked to canonical recording identifiers using the MusicBrainz canonical recording redirect table. Recordings were retained only when matching metadata and matching rows in all three AcousticBrainz feature tables (low-level, rhythm, and tonal) were available.

Cleaning and aggregation

Only AcousticBrainz submissions with submission_offset == 0 were retained. Analyses with missing or nonfinite values in any of the selected numeric acoustic features were removed before aggregation.

When multiple original recordings mapped to the same canonical recording, numeric acoustic features were combined using medians. The character variables key and scale were taken from the first retained analysis and are retained for descriptive interpretation.

Up to 25 canonical recordings per matched artist were randomly selected without replacement, using seed 20260925. Artists with fewer than 25 eligible recordings contribute all eligible recordings; artists with no eligible recordings are absent.

Use and interpretation

Acoustic features are algorithmic estimates rather than human assessments. The features have not been standardized in this dataset. Consider their different units, scales, and meanings before applying distance-based clustering.

Identifiers, artist and release information, song titles, and n_acoustic_recordings provide context or provenance and should not be treated as acoustic clustering features. In particular, n_acoustic_recordings describes how the dataset was constructed, not a characteristic of how a song sounds.

The variables key and scale are categorical musical descriptors. They may be used to interpret results but should not be supplied directly to k-means, which requires numeric input.

The artist list was deliberately selected for teaching. The dataset is not a representative sample of all music, artists, or recordings. The date of the AcousticBrainz dump indicates when the data were compiled, not when the music was recorded or released.

References

Essentia music feature documentation: https://essentia.upf.edu/streaming_extractor_music.html
